title: The man who wrote the AI-boom bible just got margin-called out of it
excerpt: The man who wrote the defining case for the AI boom just got wiped out betting on it. Situational Awareness, the hedge fund founded by former OpenAI researcher Leopold Aschenbrenner, has been forced to sell off its portfolio of public stock
content_html:
The man who wrote the defining case for the AI boom just got wiped out betting on it. Situational Awareness, the hedge fund founded by former OpenAI researcher Leopold Aschenbrenner, has been forced to sell off its portfolio of public stocks after steep losses. Ken Griffin’s Citadel has bought the lot.

The collapse was first reported by CNBC’s David Faber. The fund’s prime brokers had been scrambling to raise cash to meet margin calls, he said. The whole public book went in one enormous trade. Roughly two-thirds of the fund’s assets were public equities, held long and shorted. The Wall Street Journal reported that the rival firm Millennium had also bid for the book.

The trade that broke

The fund made one big, leveraged bet: that the AI build-out would keep lifting the companies supplying its chips, memory and power. That trade turned hard. Its positions in memory maker Micron, SK Hynix, Sandisk, Nebius and CoreWeave unravelled fast.

The damage was brutal. Nebius, where the fund disclosed a multi-billion-dollar stake in May, has fallen about 48 per cent from its peak. That erased roughly $35bn in market value. Sandisk is down 56 per cent in barely a month. The fund had also bet against software, and shorts in names like Adobe moved the wrong way, squeezing it from both sides.

It was, in effect, the long-chips, short-software trade that has defined this year, taken to an extreme with borrowed money. Leverage turned a bad month into a crisis. The Financial Times reported the fund used borrowing to magnify returns, a strategy that amplifies losses just as fast. Bank of America, Goldman Sachs and JPMorgan were left marketing its positions.

From $225m to a fire sale

The speed of the rise makes the fall more striking. Aschenbrenner launched the fund in 2024 with about $225m, backed by the Stripe founders, Nat Friedman, Daniel Gross and the trading firm Jane Street.

It grew past $20bn, and CNBC reported it swelled to as much as $45bn at the start of July. It was up 439 per cent in the first half of the year.

It ran on a skeleton crew. According to The Verge, the fund had eight employees, only four of them investment professionals. Aschenbrenner had no prior trading experience before launching it. He does have a following: more than 250,000 people on X.

The tone did not shift as the losses mounted. In a 24 July letter to investors, seen by the FT, Aschenbrenner said the fund had “not been immune” to the sell-off. He then called it one of the best buying windows since early 2025. A postscript invited clients to add fresh cash on 1 August.

Anthropic survives the wreck

One large bet is still standing. Situational Awareness keeps its private holdings, and the biggest is a stake in Anthropic, which the FT valued at about $5bn. The firm will carry on as a private investment vehicle, essentially an Anthropic holding company with a hedge fund attached.

Reports that it was shopping the Anthropic stake are “not accurate,” a spokesman told CNBC. There is a neat irony in what remains. Aschenbrenner is engaged to Avital Balwit, the chief of staff to Anthropic’s chief executive, Dario Amodei.

The oracle’s thesis on trial

This is a personal blow to one of the most watched figures in the AI trade. Aschenbrenner, now 25, was a Columbia valedictorian at 19 and worked on OpenAI’s Superalignment team before the company fired him in 2024.

His 165-page essay, “Situational Awareness,” gave the fund its name and the market its script. He declared that “the AGI race has begun,” and forecast trillion-dollar compute clusters and hundreds of millions of humming GPUs. It became the intellectual playbook for the entire infrastructure bet.

The essay was not wrong that AI needs more chips. The fund’s undoing was leverage, not the thesis, and there is a wrinkle. The very stocks it had to dump, SK Hynix and the rest, jumped sharply the next day. Some read that as a sign the forced selling had marked a short-term bottom rather than a verdict on the AI trade itself.

The comparisons wrote themselves. ZeroHedge dubbed it “Archegos 2.0,” after the family office that imploded on hidden leverage. Others reached for Three Arrows, the crypto fund that believed in its own supercycle. Commentators could not resist the obvious point, that a firm named Situational Awareness had missed the risk in its own book.

It was also, several noted, the second spectacular flame-out linked to Aschenbrenner. He once had a brief stint at Sam Bankman-Fried’s FTX philanthropy, the arm of the empire that collapsed with the crypto exchange.

One strand of the reaction deserves care. On X, traders spun a theory that Citadel had talked up a Fed rate rise to drive AI stocks lower, then bought Aschenbrenner’s book cheap. That is speculation, not established fact. What is confirmed is simpler and older: an eight-person fund used heavy leverage, the market turned, and a bigger firm picked up the pieces.

content_html_zh:
为人工智能繁荣写下定义案例的人刚刚在人工智能的赌注上破产了。 由前 OpenAI 研究员利奥波德·阿申布伦纳 (Leopold Aschenbrenner) 创立的对冲基金 Situational Awareness 在大幅亏损后被迫出售其公开股票投资组合。 肯·格里芬 (Ken Griffin) 的城堡 (Citadel) 买下了这块地。

CNBC 的 David Faber 最先报道了此次倒塌事件。 他说，该基金的主要经纪人一直在争先恐后地筹集现金以满足追加保证金的要求。 整本公开书籍进行了一笔巨大的交易。 该基金大约三分之二的资产是公开股票，持有多头和空头。 据《华尔街日报》报道，竞争对手千禧公司也竞购了这本书。

打破的贸易

该基金下了一个很大的杠杆赌注：人工智能的扩建将继续提振为其提供芯片、内存和电力的公司。 那笔交易变得艰难。 它在内存制造商美光 (Micron)、SK 海力士 (SK Hynix)、闪迪 (Sandisk)、Nebius 和 CoreWeave 中的地位迅速瓦解。

损害是残酷的。 Nebius 基金在 5 月份披露了价值数十亿美元的股份，目前已较峰值下跌约 48%。 这导致市值蒸发约 350 亿美元。 Sandisk 在不到一个月的时间里股价下跌了 56%。 该基金还做空了软件行业，而 Adob​​e 等公司的空头方向却错误，受到了双方的挤压。

实际上，今年定义的多头筹码、空头软件交易，通过借钱达到了极端。 杠杆将糟糕的一个月变成了危机。 英国《金融时报》报道称，该基金利用借款来放大回报，这一策略也同样迅速放大了损失。 美国银行、高盛和摩根大通只能推销其头寸。

从 2.25 亿美元到贱卖

上涨的速度使得下跌更加惊人。 Aschenbrenner 于 2024 年推出了该基金，资金约为 2.25 亿美元，并得到了 Stripe 创始人 Nat Friedman、Daniel Gross 和贸易公司 Jane Street 的支持。

其规模已超过 200 亿美元，据 CNBC 报道，该规模在 7 月初已增至 450 亿美元。 今年上半年上涨了439%。

它依靠骨干人员运行。 据 The Verge 报道，该基金有 8 名员工，其中只有 4 名投资专业人士。 阿申布伦纳在推出该产品之前没有任何交易经验。 他确实拥有一批追随者：X 上有超过 250,000 人。

随着损失的增加，基调并没有改变。 英国《金融时报》看到，阿申布伦纳在 7 月 24 日致投资者的一封信中表示，该基金“未能幸免”遭受抛售。 他随后称其为 2025 年初以来最佳买入窗口之一。 附言邀请客户在 8 月 1 日添加新现金。

人类在沉船中幸存下来

一笔大赌注仍然有效。 Situational Awareness 保留其私人持股，其中最大的是 Anthropic 的股份，《金融时报》对其估值约为 50 亿美元。 该公司将继续作为私人投资工具，本质上是一家附有对冲基金的 Anthropic 控股公司。

一位发言人告诉 CNBC，有关收购 Anthropic 股份的报道“不准确”。 剩下的事情有一个巧妙的讽刺。 阿申布伦纳与阿维塔尔·巴尔维特订婚，阿维塔尔·巴尔维特是 Anthropic 首席执行官达里奥·阿莫代的幕僚长。

甲骨文的审判论文

这对人工智能行业最受关注的人物之一来说是一个个人打击。 现年 25 岁的阿申布伦纳 (Aschenbrenner) 19 岁时曾在哥伦比亚大学发表告别演说，曾在 OpenAI 的 Superalignment 团队工作，后来该公司于 2024 年解雇了他。

他长达 165 页的文章《态势感知》为该基金命名，为市场命名。 他宣称“AGI 竞赛已经开始”，并预测价值数万亿美元的计算集群和数亿个嗡嗡作响的 GPU。 它成为整个基础设施投资的智力手册。

这篇文章认为人工智能需要更多芯片并没有错。 该基金的失败是杠杆作用，而不是理论，而且有一个问题。 第二天，它不得不抛售的SK海力​​士和其他公司的股票大幅上涨。 一些人认为，这是强制抛售标志着短期底部的一个迹象，而不是对人工智能交易本身的判决。

比较是自己写的。 ZeroHedge 将其称为“Archegos 2.0”，以纪念因隐藏杠杆而崩溃的家族办公室。 其他人则选择了“三箭”，这是一家相信自己超级周期的加密货币基金。 评论家们无法抗拒一个显而易见的观点，那就是一家名为“态势感知”的公司在自己的书中忽略了风险。

一些人指出，这也是与阿申布伦纳有关的第二次壮观的熄火。 他曾在 Sam Bankman-Fried 的 FTX 慈善事业中短暂任职，该慈善事业是随着加密货币交易所而崩溃的帝国的一部分。

其中一个反应值得关注。 在 X 上，交易员提出了这样一个理论：Citadel 曾大肆宣扬美联储加息，以推低人工智能股票，然后低价买入了 Aschenbrenner 的书。 这只是猜测，并非既定事实。 已证实的事情更为简单和古老：一家八人基金使用了高杠杆，市场发生逆转，一家更大的公司收拾残局。
